Aladdin  is one of those movies that just sticks with you because it’s wild, loud, and honestly pretty funny. The Genie is all over the place, He’s easily one of the funniest parts of the movie. But when you actually pay attention to the story, there’s something kind of weird going on with Princess Jasmine. She’s supposed to be this rebellious princess who wants to make her own choices, but she barely gets to control what happens in her own story. Jasmine talks a lot about wanting freedom and not wanting someone else to choose her future, but the movie doesn’t really give her much room to do anything about it. Her dad is trying to decide who she should marry, Jafar is constantly trying to control everything, and even Aladdin spends most of the movie lying to her. Jasmine tries to stand up for herself, but the story keeps moving around her. It’s like she’s talking, but nobody is really listening. Another thing I noticed is how much everyone in Agrabah is constantly talking, singing, arguing, or making deals. There’s always something happening. Meanwhile, Jasmine feels like she gets pushed into the background. She has important things to say, but the movie seems more interested in Aladdin, Genie, Jafar, and all the chaos happening around them. It almost feels like Jasmine is there, but her voice gets lost in all the noise. That’s also what makes the movie kind of absurd. The whole world is crazy with magic carpets, a talking parrot, a magical lamp, and a Genie who can basically do anything. The rules don’t always make much sense, but that’s part of what makes it fun. Everyone is chasing something, whether it’s power, freedom, love, or just getting what they want. Jasmine wants freedom, but she doesn’t really get to figure out what that means for herself. Overall, I still think Aladdin is a really fun movie. The animation is colorful, the music is memorable, and Genie brings so much energy to the movie. I just wish Jasmine had more control over her own story because she actually has the potential to be one of the strongest characters. Instead, she sometimes feels like she’s just reacting to whatever Aladdin, Jafar, or her dad does next.

A young man thieves to survive in the small city he lives in. One day, he runs into a woman on the streets, who is actually the princess. During this time, the king is courting princes from around the world to marry her, but she isn’t interested in any of them. Meanwhile, the kings guard is plotting his takeover and wants to build an empire. When the thief is caught sneaking into the palace, he is assigned by the kings guard to visit a magic genie and make his wishes come true. He makes a wish to have the title and appearance as a prince so he can win over the princess. When he gets invited to the kingdom, at first he makes himself out to be an idiot. Afterwards, he is able to charm her when he sneaks into her palace and take her out to see the city. The next day, the king guard discovers what he did and sends him away. However, the princess is able to bring him back by making a wish. The genie gets freed and the thief and the princess live happily.

Another classic from my youth, and this was mostly well done.  I loved seeing Agrabah come to life! Makes me want to travel to this part of the world!  The casting was good too - loved what Naomi Scott and Mena Massoud brought.  I was skeptical of Will Smith heading into this just because of how iconic Robin Williams version was, but I liked how he played the genie Did I mishear the line in the market where Aladdin and Jasmine first met? Did he just say “trust me” and not “do you trust me?” I know I’ve complained about the changing of line deliveries with these remakes but the importance of that line to coincide with later in the movie…it’s not like Disney to miss that Otherwise my main complaint is the songs were flat compared to the original again. Naomi Scott has been the best and closest to the original of the films I’ve seen thus far.  I get it, the original had broadway singers but..well this is a musical, right?

Will Smith had the hardest job in the world stepping into the shoes of the late Robin Williams, but he wisely didn't try to copy him. Instead, Smith brought his own 90s Fresh Prince charisma, hip-hop energy, and charm, making Genie his own. The production design is colorful, festive, and theatrical. The grand parade sequence for "Friend Like Me" and "Prince Ali" is pure Bollywood-inspired spectacle that translates surprisingly well to live-action. Marwan Kenzari’s Jafar is unfortunately pretty forgettable. Instead of the sinister, imposing villain from the animated classic, he comes across as a bit too young and mild-mannered

𖦹°‧Honestly, this was way more fun than I expected. Will Smith’s Genie completely stole the movie for me—he doesn’t try to be Robin Williams, he just does his own thing, and somehow it work. Naomi Scott was also easily one of the best parts, and “Speechless” was genuinely one of my favorite additions. The visuals, costumes, dancing, and music made everything feel so colorful and magical, even when the movie got a little cheesy. My biggest problem was Jafar; he just didn’t feel intimidating enough. and I never really bought him as the big villain. Still, I had a great time watching this, and honestly… I’d watch it again𖦹°‧

A retelling of the classic animated movie that has the spectacle but lacks the dazzling splendor that made the original film timeless.  This film adds a bit more depth to Agrabah as well as some exposition on Aladdin’s parents and Jasmine’s mother.  The acting was unfortunately the film’s weakest point and Will Smith is no Robin Williams but he does try to do something different.  Overall not a great live action adaptation but certainly not the worst.  Fun at times and the set pieces and wardrobe was beautiful, but this was no diamond in the rough.

Mena and Naomi are so talented and the perfect casting for Aladdin and Jasmine! Their voices are perfect together. The costume and set design are phenomenal, but a huge portion of the movie is too dark to see any of it. The CGI isn't the best for a movie that relies so heavily on it but I appreciate the use of CGI rather than animal actors throughout. Giving Jasmine a song was genius, Speechless is amazing. This movie does seem to presume the audience is familiar with the original story since the plot isn't as clear.
